The **Section on Intergovernmental Administration and Management** (SIAM) invites scholars and practitioners to submit proposals for papers to be presented at the 13th Annual Deil S. Wright Symposium. The symposium is a full day event that honors the career and contributions of Professor Deil S. Wright, a charter member of SIAM who remained active until his passing in 2009. The Wright Symposium will be held Friday, April 9, 2027, 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. during the national conference of the American Society for Public Administration (ASPA) in New Orleans, Louisiana.

**Conference Theme:** Navigating Multilevel Governance: Adaptation, Tension, and Innovation in Intergovernmental Relations

The ASPA Section on Intergovernmental Administration and Management (SIAM) invites scholars, practitioners, and early-career researchers to submit paper abstracts, panel proposals, and workshop concepts for the upcoming ASPA Annual Conference.

As public policy challenges become increasingly complex and cross-jurisdictional, traditional models of federalism and intergovernmental relations face unprecedented stress. SIAM seeks high-quality proposals that explore how federal, state, local, and tribal governments negotiate authority, share resources, and deliver public services in a dynamic policy environment.

We encourage submissions addressing, but not limited to the following core tracks:

- Power & Jurisdiction – Preemption, state-local home rule, state AG litigation, and judicial federalism.
- Regionalism and Collaborative Governance – Regional Councils of Government (COGs), special districts, cross-sector partnerships, and metropolitan service sharing.
- Fiscal Dynamics – Grant administration, unfunded mandates, formula shifts, and local tax capacity in today's political and economic environment.
- Sovereignty and Multilevel Partnerships – Tribal-state relations, federal trust responsibilities, and the co-management of natural resources.
- Data Governance and Technology Regulatory Frontiers – AI and data privacy regulation, cross-jurisdictional data sharing, smart cities, and infrastructure deployment.
- Doctoral Student Panel – Doctoral student research on intergovernmental relations and government innovation.

## Submission Guidelines

- **Abstract Length**: 250–400 words
- **Required Information**: Title, author name(s), institutional affiliation(s), contact email, and designated track (*or indicate if you would like your abstract considered for the doctoral student panel*).
- **Submission deadline**: October 9, 2026

**Please submit abstracts to:**

- Jered Carr, University of Illinois Chicago - [jbcarr@uic.edu](mailto:jbcarr@uic.edu)
- Chris Goodman, Northern Illinois University - [cgoodman@niu.edu](mailto:cgoodman@niu.edu)
- Mitch Berg, Indiana University Bloomington - [bergmi@iu.edu](mailto:bergmi@iu.edu)
- Jayce Farmer, University of Nevada, Las Vegas - [jayce.farmer@unlv.edu](mailto:jayce.farmer@unlv.edu)
